title: Cover Design: Journals and Technical Publications
slide_intent: Teach editors to establish recurring positions for a technical publication’s identity and reference information so readers can find it from issue to issue.
strategic_value: NASA can make a technical series recognizable while giving research data and diagrams enough room to be read.
demonstration: The examples pair a spare NASA Tech Briefs front cover with a technical page containing a boxed diagram. A smaller NASA Facts page appears below.
practical_value: Give center accreditation and the headline clear positions, keep catalog numbers in a consistent location and use a box to distinguish a technical diagram.

content_islands.name: Cover guidance
content_islands.spec: Place the section title at left and explain the use of the logotype within a series title in the neighboring columns.

content_islands.name: Tech Briefs specimens
content_islands.spec: Align the mostly open front cover with the information-dense technical page. Keep their captions and common masthead visible.

content_islands.name: NASA Facts specimen
content_islands.spec: Place the smaller example beneath the cover. Show the center identification, photograph and two-column text as one publication page.
